evidence:
Main source: Morwani, Edelman, Oncescu, Zhao, Kakade, "Feature emergence via margin maximization" (ICLR 2024, arXiv 2311.07568; already in refs.bib as morwani2024feature). I read the PDF v2. Its Introduction, paragraph 1, says: "The research area of mechanistic interpretability (Olah et al., 2020; Elhage et al., 2021; Olsson et al., 2022; Elhage et al., 2022) aims to dissect individual trained neural networks ... identifying and interpreting sub-circuits ... Mechanistic interpretability analyses typically leave open the question of why the observed representations arise as a result of training." Their abstract adds: "this paper explores a complementary question -- why do networks arrive at particular computational strategies?"

Our sentence is a near-paraphrase of that line, so it should carry the citation.

Secondary source: Sharkey et al. 2025, "Open Problems in Mechanistic Interpretability" (arXiv 2501.16496; read in full HTML). Sec 2.1.2(d) says "exploring theories about why neural networks generalize appears to be a promising avenue" and calls for "a more dynamic, developmental view of how mechanistic structure emerges in the training process". Sec 3.3.2 treats forecasting capabilities that arise during training as open.

For "finds the circuits": Olah et al. 2020, Zoom In (Distill, doi 10.23915/distill.00024.001; metadata fetched), and Elhage et al. 2021, A Mathematical Framework for Transformer Circuits (fetched).

Checked and not useful: Bereska & Gavves (TMLR 2024, arXiv 2404.14082). The fetched abstract does not frame why circuits form as an open problem.

Notes are in /Users/ruhaanrajadhyaksha/projects/grok/heracles/paper/litcheck/items/f5-why-circuits/CHECK.md.

recommended_citations.why: Intro para 1 contains almost the same sentence: 'Mechanistic interpretability analyses typically leave open the question of why the observed representations arise as a result of training.' This supports the whole claim and attributes the wording.
Canonical reference for 'mechanistic interpretability finds the circuits networks implement'.
Circuits in transformers. Backs the 'finds the circuits' half of the sentence.
Optional. Sec 2.1.2(d) names theories of why networks generalize and a developmental view of how mechanistic structure emerges in training as underdeveloped directions. Supports 'leaves open'.

recommended_change: Change the sentence to: "Mechanistic interpretability finds the circuits trained networks implement \citep{olah2020zoom,elhage2021mathematical,nanda2023progress}, but typically leaves open \emph{why} they arise \citep{morwani2024feature}." Morwani et al. is cited in the very next sentence, so another option is: "As \citet{morwani2024feature} observe, mechanistic interpretability finds the circuits ... but typically leaves open why they arise." The wording is almost Morwani's own, so leaving it unattributed would look like borrowed text.
